subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host allowlist entries authorize non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback, or did current main intentionally retire that contract after the SSRF hardening?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible security tradeoffs, and the linked fix PR could relax the SSRF boundary beyond the original failing test if the contract is not settled first.

options.title: Confirm strict loopback blocking
options.body: Treat current main's test change as the intended resolution and close or revise the linked PR so non-localhost loopback DNS rebinding remains blocked.

options.title: Approve a narrow browser exception
options.body: Allow only the approved browser loopback-alias case while keeping metadata and link-local DNS-answer checks intact.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the related private-network confirmation and allowlist model is decided together.

recommendation.title: Confirm strict loopback blocking
recommendation.body: Treat current main's test change as the intended resolution and close or revise the linked PR so non-localhost loopback DNS rebinding remains blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened this issue and appear in the merged SSRF hardening provenance, so they are the best available owner for the contract decision.
